remarks: A customer and a companion came to buy the top XEV 9e (called 9e Pack Three) in the Ruby Velvet colour, with two chargers and accessories, and wanted about 30.50 lakh all in and delivery at once. Said aloud by the rep: ex-showroom 30.50 lakh at launch, 31.25 lakh with the 11 kW charger (the charger is worth 75,000); a scheme discount of 2 lakh (1.5 lakh from the company and 50,000 from the dealer), called final; TCS 31,250; RTO about 38,300; insurance 1+2 at about 1 lakh 7 thousand and 3+3 at about 1 lakh 52 thousand; a 25,000 accessory pack; a 60,000 extended warranty the customer did not want; on-road 31 lakh 7 thousand (13:33) and later 31.89 lakh as the final figure (16:08). The customer worked the total out as 31.19 lakh with accessories and 30.94 lakh without, and asked for a round 30.50 or 31. The rep said a further 10 to 20 thousand might come off after talking (23:02) and that he would have to put in a request to the company (23:18), and also that he would not ask for more because the company had already given 50,000 (20:54). Ruby Velvet is not in stock: about two weeks, which the customer said does not work; the rep offered the white or black he has in stock (33:30, 44:22). The customer side phoned a contact at an Ahmedabad showroom (big stock, about 300 cars, SG Highway) who they said gives more discount, and said they would go there (39:04). The customer lives in an apartment with no way to charge at home; the rep and the companion explained charging at a workplace or on the road. A quotation was to be sent on WhatsApp (29:49 to 29:52). No booking was made and no test drive was done (a 9e was seen on the road). The rep gives his own name as Joshi and his mobile number (23:34, 24:08). Speaker labels in this recording are not reliable in places; where a line could be from either side the translation says so.
